title: Numerical nearness preserves tangent standard-basis degrees without reducedness
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$, with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].
Assume no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$, where a minimal prime contains no strictly smaller prime. Let $z\in\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ be over $\mathfrak m$ and belong to the chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/\bar x_0]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Put
$$D_T=T[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(x_0t_i-x_i:1\leq i\leq r),\qquad T'=(D_T)_{\mathfrak p'},$$
where $\mathfrak p'$ is the inverse image of $z$ under the surjection $D_T\twoheadrightarrow R[I/\bar x_0]$, $t_i\mapsto\bar x_i/\bar x_0$. Assume $T'$ is regular local, let $R_z=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R),z}$, and put $\mathfrak a'=\ker(T'\twoheadrightarrow R_z)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
For a regular local ring $(V,\mathfrak l,\kappa)$ and an ideal $\mathfrak b\subseteq\mathfrak l$, let $E(V,\mathfrak b)=\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}V\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l/\mathfrak b}(V/\mathfrak b))$. Define $\nu^*(V,\mathfrak b)$ to be the nondecreasing sequence containing $d$ with multiplicity $\dim_\kappa(E_d/(\sum_{j=1}^d (\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}V)_j E_{d-j}))$, followed by infinitely many $\infty$'s. Equivalently these are the degrees of a minimal homogeneous generating set of $E$, padded by $\infty$.
Put $h_R(n)=\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1})$ and $h_z(n)=\operatorname{length}_{R_z}(R_z/\mathfrak n_z^{n+1})$, where $\mathfrak n_z$ is the maximal ideal of $R_z$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Set $\delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(z)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] and $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$. If $\Lambda^\delta h_z=h_R$, then
$$\nu^*(T',\mathfrak a')=\nu^*(T,\mathfrak a).$$
No converse is asserted. No reducedness hypothesis is imposed on $R$.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2), pp.155-156, Theorem III, p.156, and its proof, p.187. The basic assumptions concern an arbitrary closed subscheme X of a regular scheme Z, with regular normally flat center D; X need not be reduced. Local regular-ambient chart form. Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this specialized theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normal-flat-double-initial-ideal], which has no reducedness assumption: the specified parameter map gives $S=B/C$ with $C=\ker\beta$, and $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R=S[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$, with ambient tangent ideal $Ck[X,Y]$. The graded-length bridge identifies $h_R(n)$ with the sum of dimensions in degrees at most $n$. Write $h_S(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n\dim_k S_j$. Adding one degree-one polynomial variable replaces this cumulative function by $\Lambda h_S$: in degree $d$, the monomials in that variable give $\bigoplus_{a=0}^d S_{d-a}Y^a$. Iterating gives $h_R=\Lambda^s h_S$. Likewise the degree-$d$ minimal-generator quotient of $Ck[X,Y]$ is that of $C$: reduction modulo the positive-degree ideal kills all terms with a $Y$ factor and all positive-degree multiples in $B$. Thus $\nu^*(T,\mathfrak a)=\nu_B(C)$, with the multiplicity formula of the projective-cone node.

source.place: Section 2, p.153, and paragraph following Example (4.2), p.157; online source https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED

proof.text: Put $\boldsymbol u=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_s)\subset T'$ and $\overline V=T'/(\boldsymbol u)$. Apply the permissible-coordinate-chart statement to the full parameter boundary and to the centre generated by all the $x_i$. Take the boundary to include all the $x_i$ and $y_j$; this applies only to the regular ambient ring $T$, not to its possibly nonreduced quotient $R$. Since $z$ lies over $\mathfrak m$, all members of $\boldsymbol u$ vanish there and occur at distinct positions in a regular system of parameters of $T'$. The ambient chart presentation gives $\overline V=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p}=Q$, where $\mathfrak p$ is the point in the exceptional affine fibre chart. For the quotient transform, relative-Proj base change identifies its closed fibre with $\operatorname{Proj}S$: degree by degree its Rees algebra tensored with $k$ is $I^d/\mathfrak m I^d$, also the degree-$d$ piece of $G\otimes_A k$, since $I^{d+1}\subseteq\mathfrak m I^d$. On the $X_0$ chart the degree-zero fractions are $f/X_0^{\deg f}$, represented by $f(1,t)$; hence the fibre local ring is exactly $F=Q/J$ from the projective-cone node, and $R_z/(\boldsymbol u)R_z=F$. The induced ambient ideal is $\mathfrak a'Q=J$. These identifications send each $t_i$ to the same named ratio and preserve the residue field, so $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(F)=\delta$.

source.place: Section 2, p.154; Remark (5.2), p.158; chart notation (13.1), pp.168--169; online source https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED

proof.text:
Apply the linear-section comparison to $V=T'$, $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak a'$ and the $s+1$ distinct parameters $\boldsymbol u$. It gives $h_z\leq\Lambda^{s+1}h_F$. Apply the projective-cone comparison to $C\subset B$ and $\mathfrak p$; it gives $\Lambda^{\delta+1}h_F\leq h_S$. Finite summation preserves pointwise inequalities. Consequently
$$\Lambda^\delta h_z\ \leq\ \Lambda^{\delta+s+1}h_F\ \leq\ \Lambda^s h_S=h_R.$$
The hypothesis identifies the two endpoints, so equality holds at each term for every $n$. Summation is injective on functions on $\mathbf N$: recover $f(0)$ from $\Lambda f(0)$ and $f(n)$ from $\Lambda f(n)-\Lambda f(n-1)$ for $n>0$. Cancel $\Lambda^\delta$ from the first equality and $\Lambda^s$ from the second. This gives $h_z=\Lambda^{s+1}h_F$ and $\Lambda^{\delta+1}h_F=h_S$.

source.place: Inequalities (4.1), p.156; proof of Theorem III, p.187; online source https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED

proof.text:
The first equality activates the equality clause of the linear-section node, so $
u^*(T',\mathfrak a')=
u^*(Q,J)$. The second activates the equality clause of the projective-cone node, so $
u^*(Q,J)=
u_B(C)$. Step 1 identified $
u_B(C)=
u^*(T,\mathfrak a)$. Chaining these three equalities proves the stated conclusion, including the multiplicities of all finite degrees and the padded infinite tail.

source.place: Remark (12.2), pp.167--168; proof of Theorem III, p.187; online source https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED

lean.statement: theorem permissibleBlowupStandardDegrees {T : Type u} [CommRing T] [IsRegularLocalRing T] (r s : ℕ) (x : Fin (r + 1) → T) (y : Fin s → T) (hparams : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y)) (b : Ideal T) (hb : b ≤ Ideal.span (Set.range x)) (hflat : Module.Flat ((T ⧸ b) ⧸ (Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk b)) (Ideal.associatedGraded ((Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk b)))) (hmin : ∀ q ∈ minimalPrimes (T ⧸ b), ¬ (Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk b) ≤ q) (ρ : ParameterChart x →+* chartRing ((Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk b)) (Ideal.Quotient.mk b (x 0))) (hρ : IsQuotientChartMap x b ρ) (z : PrimeSpectrum (chartRing ((Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk b)) (Ideal.Quotient.mk b (x 0)))) (hz : z.asIdeal.comap ((algebraMap (T ⧸ b) _).comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk b)) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal T) [IsRegularLocalRing (LocalChart ρ z)] (κ : IsLocalRing.ResidueField T →+* z.asIdeal.ResidueField) (hκ : ∀ t : T, κ (IsLocalRing.residue T t) = algebraMap _ z.asIdeal.ResidueField (algebraMap (T ⧸ b) (chartRing ((Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk b)) (Ideal.Quotient.mk b (x 0))) (Ideal.Quotient.mk b t))) (hnear : letI := κ.toAlgebra (HilbertSamuel.summation^[Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (IsLocalRing.ResidueField T) z.asIdeal.ResidueField)]) (fun n ↦ (Module.length (Localization.AtPrime z.asIdeal) ((Localization.AtPrime z.asIdeal) ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime z.asIdeal) ^ (n + 1))).toNat) = quotientHilbertFunction (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal T) b) : nuStar (transformIdeal ρ z) = nuStar b
lean.note: Reuses the published Hironaka chart and numerical constructions. The point is represented by its prime in the specified affine chart. rho is fixed on coefficients and all ratios by IsQuotientChartMap; kappa is the unique residue-field map fixed by hκ. Neither is an arbitrary replacement map. No reducedness or rationality hypothesis is added.
